# New-ZbxValueMap

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a value map.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxValueMap [[-Name] <string>] [-HostId <ulong>] [-Uuid <string>] [-Mapping <ZabbixValueMapMappingRequest[]>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A value map turns raw item values into words, such as 1 into Up and 0 into Down, for the frontend and notifications. The New-ZbxValueMap cmdlet sends valuemap.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new value map back with valuemap.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -Mapping; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. A host or template piped from Get-ZbxHost or Get-ZbxTemplate binds -HostId, so one command creates a value map on each. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a value map

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' | New-ZbxValueMap -Name 'Service state' -Mapping @{ value = '0'; newvalue = 'Down' }, @{ value = '1'; newvalue = 'Up' }
```

Creates a value map named Service state on the host web-01. The command writes the new value map, read back from the server.

### Example 2: Create a value map on every host of a group

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Group 'Linux servers' | New-ZbxValueMap -Name 'Service state' -Mapping @{ value = '0'; newvalue = 'Down' }, @{ value = '1'; newvalue = 'Up' }
```

A host piped from Get-ZbxHost binds -HostId, so every host of the group Linux servers gets its own value map.
